comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED — my first read of this ticket was WRONG and is retracted here.

I initially read `fetch-secrets.sh:153-157` ("All-blank => {"tokens": []} ... fails-closed until
an operator populates >=1 PAT") and concluded this was `environment-or-config`: an unpopulated
SSM slot, no code defect, operator action only. Evidence says otherwise. The SSM parameters ARE
populated — all three, and they predate the crash:

  /rebar/prod/mcp-client-pat-copilot  SecureString  2026-08-25T16:42:56Z
  /rebar/prod/mcp-client-pat-codex    SecureString  2026-08-25T16:42:57Z
  /rebar/prod/mcp-client-pat-claude   SecureString  2026-08-25T16:42:58Z

(listed via get-parameters-by-path WITHOUT decryption; no values read or printed)

THE ACTUAL MECHANISM — a time skew, not a missing secret
An on-box measurement at 16:44:59Z, two minutes AFTER the PATs landed in SSM, printed
`token_records= 0 []` — the on-disk mcp-static-tokens.json was still `{"tokens": []}`. A manual
`fetch-secrets.sh` run at 16:45:45Z then printed `token_records= 3 ['copilot','codex','claude']`.
Populating an SSM SecureString advances no git ref, and nothing regenerates the on-disk file on
its own. So: PATs land 16:42Z -> file stays empty -> an unrelated src/rebar change on main
triggers the mcp blue-green path -> the new container bind-mounts the STALE empty file -> fails
closed at `_mcp_auth.py:725`.

The error string is itself the discriminator. "defines no tokens" is the empty-ARRAY branch
(line 725). Had the records been present but the env vars missing, the error would have been
line 766 ("'token_env' names env var ... unset or empty"). It was not — so the file was empty,
not the environment.

Why the LIVE container works while new ones failed: `compose-mcp-1` was force-recreated at
16:55Z, ten minutes AFTER the manual fetch-secrets run rewrote the file. Same path, same mount —
the containers differ only in WHEN they started. Ruled out: a different mount path
(autodeploy.sh:365 mounts the same $COMPOSE_DIR file) and missing env (autodeploy.sh:352 passes
the same --env-file). Both were candidate explanations and both are refuted by the code.

TWO LANDABLE REPO DEFECTS (so this is a code fix, not just an operator action)

Defect A — the mcp blue-green path never refreshes SSM-sourced secrets.
`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:621-700` does git checkout -> rsync -> build -> mcp_run_new and
calls fetch-secrets.sh ZERO times, yet it consumes two rsync-EXCLUDED, SSM-materialized
artifacts: `.env` (autodeploy.sh:352) and `mcp-static-tokens.json` (autodeploy.sh:365). The
review-bot path already does exactly the right thing at autodeploy.sh:579, with a comment at
:574-578 explaining why it is required ("so new/rotated keys reach the container without a manual
boot ... .env is rsync-EXCLUDED + SSM-sourced, so it is otherwise never regenerated on deploy").
The mcp path was never given the same treatment. fetch-secrets is invoked only under the guard at
autodeploy.sh:506, keyed on SECRETS_PATHS changing (autodeploy.sh:147) — and autodeploy.sh:144-146
states the gap outright: "A pure SSM VALUE rotation with no git change does not advance main, so
autodeploy no-ops on it."

Defect B — the live working config is not reproducible from git and is self-destructing.
`REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL` exists ONLY as a line an operator hand-appended to
/opt/rebar/infra/compose/.env at 16:55Z. It is absent from the mcp `environment:` block and from
mcp_run_new's -e list. fetch-secrets.sh regenerates .env WHOLESALE (mktemp + mv -f) and its
heredoc does not emit that key — so the next fetch-secrets run DELETES the operator's fix and
reverts the box to the 16:5xZ failure. Note the trap: fixing Defect A alone would TRIGGER Defect
B, because A's whole point is to run fetch-secrets on every mcp deploy. They must land together.

Correction to the ticket's Summary: the compose file at docker-compose.yml:349-352 does carry a
`${REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL:-https://...}` default with a comment citing bug
haughty-leisured-puffer. That default only applies to compose's own `environment:` interpolation;
mcp_run_new builds its own -e list and does not inherit it, which is why the blue-green container
still lacked the value.

STILL UNDETERMINED (read-only limit): the alarm is STILL in ALARM and re-alarmed at 2026-08-26
01:13Z, long after both known causes were satisfied on disk. deploy_errors datapoints continue
(00:28Z, 00:43Z, 01:15Z, 01:30Z). Both known causes appear resolved on disk, so a THIRD failure
may be active. Confirming it needs `journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy` on the box, which requires
an SSM send-command — a mutation, so out of scope without approval. Flagging rather than guessing.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CORRECTION #2 — "Defect B" does not exist. Retracting it before it reaches a change.

My previous comment listed a second defect: that `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL` "appears nowhere in
infra/" and exists only as an operator's hand-appended .env line that fetch-secrets would wipe.
That is FALSE. I verified directly:

  infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:351
    REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL: "${REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL:-https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp}"
  infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:360
    -e "REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL=${REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL:-https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp}"

Both surfaces carry it, with the SAME non-empty default, so a blue-green container gets a valid
issuer URL from git with no .env line at all. There is even existing coverage pinning it:
tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py:72-80 asserts the mcp service env defines a non-empty
REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL. The claim came from a faulty grep; it does not survive a direct read.

Consequences for the story:
1. The operator's 16:55Z `env_file` injection was REDUNDANT, not load-bearing. The default
   already covered it. What actually recovered the box was the 16:45:45Z manual `fetch-secrets.sh`
   run that rewrote mcp-static-tokens.json with 3 records; the 16:55Z `--force-recreate` merely
   started a container that read the now-good file. The ticket's Summary attributes the recovery
   to the env_file injection — that attribution is wrong.
2. There is therefore NO "un-versioned live config that will self-destruct". fetch-secrets
   regenerating .env without that key is harmless, because the key is not needed in .env.
3. The stated risk that "fixing Defect A would TRIGGER Defect B" is void. Defect A is safe to
   land alone.

So this ticket reduces to exactly ONE landable defect — Defect A: the mcp blue-green path
(autodeploy.sh:621-700) never calls fetch-secrets.sh, so an SSM secret rotation never reaches a
new container. The review-bot path already does this correctly at autodeploy.sh:579. That single
change is sufficient to explain the incident and prevent recurrence: with it, the PATs populated
at 16:42Z would have been materialized on the very next deploy instead of requiring a human.

The ticket's title and AC list still mention the un-versioned issuer fix; those ACs are dropped
as based on a false premise. Remaining AC: the mcp deploy path refreshes SSM-sourced secrets
before starting the new container, with fail-fast semantics matching the bot path.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Patchset 2 (Gerrit 2230) — LLM-Review +1 on patchset 1; this patchset fixes the Verified -1.

MY FIX WAS A REAL REGRESSION IN THE TEST HARNESS, and I want that recorded rather than
smoothed over. Adding the fetch-secrets call to the mcp blue-green path made 10 of the 16
tests in tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py fail: the fake box never provisioned a
fetch-secrets.sh (it had no reason to — until this change the mcp path never called one), so
every simulated deploy aborted at mcp-secrets-fetch-failed before reaching its assertions.

A subagent investigating this reported the failures as PRE-EXISTING, having 'verified' it by
restoring files from HEAD — but HEAD already contained my commit, so that check could not
have detected my own regression. I re-tested against origin/main directly: 15 of 16 passed
there. The failures were mine.

FIX: the mcp fixtures now provision the same fetch-secrets.sh stub the bot-path fixtures
already use — the fake box modelling the real box, not an assertion being relaxed. Added
test_secrets_fetch_failure_aborts_before_touching_the_live_upstream, which pins the ordering
that makes the change safe: an SSM failure aborts while the OLD container is still serving.
Mutation-checked — removing the fetch-secrets call turns it RED.

Side effect worth noting: this also unblocked the compose-parity test that the sibling
store-provisioning change needed, which had never been exercisable end-to-end in this
environment for the same reason.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CLOSE BLOCKED — and my own AC was false. Recording both.

The completion verifier FAILED this ticket, on the criterion asserting rebar-autodeploy-errors
was OK with deploy_errors 0.0 across the preceding 30 minutes. The verifier was RIGHT and I was
wrong: a 5-minute-period query straddled a deploy_errors = 2.0 at 07:12Z. I reported a green
reading from a window that happened to miss the failure. That criterion is corrected and
REOPENED; this ticket does not close on a claim I cannot support.

Worth naming separately: the alarm being OK is not evidence of healthy deploys here.
rebar-autodeploy-errors is Sum over 900s requiring 3-of-4 datapoints with notBreaching on
missing data, so an ISOLATED deploy failure cannot trip it by construction. I had been treating
that green alarm as confirmation.

The deeper reason this ticket cannot yet be closed: the fix merged at 06:47Z (30d7059f632d) is
NOT RUNNING on the box. Root cause filed as carefree-swift-scallop — autodeploy.sh:541 exits 0
on a review-bot deferral, so the mcp blue-green block at :616 (which documents itself as
INDEPENDENT of the bot block) is never reached. A shared src/rebar change matches BOTH triggers,
so a busy bot silently skips the mcp deploy. Live probe confirms it: the deployed server still
returns the OLD behaviour.

There is a circularity here that is worth stating plainly, because it bounds what this ticket
can achieve on its own: THIS ticket's fix is the mcp deploy fix, and it cannot deploy because of
carefree-swift-scallop. And my own push volume is part of the chain — saturating the
single-worker review bot keeps in_flight > 0, which is what keeps autodeploy deferring.

This ticket stays in_progress until the merged fix is confirmed RUNNING, not merely merged.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The blue-green autodeploy of the `mcp` target is crash-looping on a fail-closed auth check, and
the box is currently serving a **hand-patched container whose fix is not in git**. The next
successful deploy will revert that patch and re-break the service.

`rebar-autodeploy-errors` is IN ALARM (confirmed 2026-08-25 via `describe-alarms`, us-east-1).

## Evidence

Verbatim from SSM invocation `0d3b8b4b` (2026-08-25T16:37:45Z):

    rebar._mcp_auth.AuthConfigError: static tokens file '/run/secrets/mcp-static-tokens.json' defines no tokens
      File "/app/src/rebar/mcp_server.py", line 774, in main
        server = build_server(cfg)
      File "/app/src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py", line 725, in _load_static_tokens

This is the documented fail-closed posture at `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:367-371`.

Consequence, from invocation `448230fe`:

    AUTODEPLOY_ERROR {"reason": "mcp-unhealthy", "detail": "new mcp container rebar-mcp-d49466b5e960-8092 failed /health within 120s; removing it, leaving the OLD upstream live"}
    AUTODEPLOY_ERROR {"reason": "deploy_failed", "detail": "target=d49466b5e960... fail#9 backoff=900s"}

An operator recovered manually at 16:55Z by injecting `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL` via `env_file`
and running `compose recreate` (invocation `d1d2ce4a` — "HEALTHY at t=8",
"Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8091"). A live probe confirms
`GET https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp` returns `HTTP 401 invalid_token`, so it is serving.

## Why this is urgent

1. The running config is out-of-band. The `env_file` injection is not committed, so it is one
   successful autodeploy away from being lost.
2. The deployed code is stale: the box serves `d49466b5e960`, four commits behind `main` HEAD at
   the time of investigation.
3. `fail#9 backoff=900s` means the loop is still retrying and still failing.

This is INDEPENDENT of the missing-tickets-store defect — it explains why the deployed code is
stale, not why `fsck` reports an uninitialized store. Neither causes the other.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Revised** — the original set rested on a premise since retracted (see below).

The original AC1 asked that "the operator's manual REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL fix be captured in
git so a deploy reproduces it rather than reverting it". That criterion is VOID: the value was
already supplied from git by BOTH `docker-compose.yml` and `mcp_run_new`, each with the same
default, and `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` already pinned it. The operator's hand-added
`.env` line was redundant, not load-bearing, and there was nothing to capture. See the
"CORRECTION #2" comment. Ticking it would have claimed work that was never needed.

The real, single defect and its criteria:

- [x] The mcp blue-green deploy path re-materializes its SSM-sourced secrets before starting the
      replacement container, so a rotated credential reaches it without a manual operator run.
      Delivered: `fetch-secrets.sh` is invoked in the mcp block of `autodeploy.sh`, before the
      build and well before `mcp_run_new`.
- [x] The refresh is FAIL-FAST with the same semantics as the review-bot path: an SSM error
      aborts the deploy while the OLD container is still serving, rather than replacing a
      working container using stale secrets. Delivered: `mcp-secrets-fetch-failed`.
- [x] A secrets-refresh failure is distinguishable in the error signal from a generic
      `mcp-unhealthy`. Delivered: its own named reason, asserted by
      `test_secrets_fetch_failure_aborts_before_touching_the_live_upstream`.
- [x] Regression coverage pins the ORDERING that makes it safe (refresh strictly before the new
      container starts), and the structural check pins that the call exists at all:
      `test_mcp_bluegreen_refreshes_ssm_secrets_before_starting_the_new_container`.
- [ ] `rebar-autodeploy-errors` is OK **and the fix has actually deployed**. NOT YET MET, and
      my earlier claim here was WRONG: I asserted `deploy_errors` was 0.0 across the
      preceding 30 minutes, but a 5-minute-period query straddled a `deploy_errors = 2.0`
      at 07:12Z. The completion verifier failed this criterion and was right to. The alarm
      reads OK only because it needs 3-of-4 900s datapoints, so an isolated failure cannot
      trip it by construction — a green alarm is not evidence of a healthy deploy here.
      This criterion stays OPEN until the merged fix is confirmed running on the box.

## Completion evidence (merged origin/main 30d7059f632d)

Landed as Gerrit 2230 with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1. Both new tests were mutation-checked:
removing the `fetch-secrets.sh` call turns each RED, and restoring it turns them GREEN.

Provision the fetch-secrets stub the fake box now needs, and pin the fail-fast ordering
Structural check that the mcp block calls fetch-secrets.sh before mcp_run_new
